prompt.context: DevCo is a global medical device manufacturer headquartered in the US with operations in more than 60 countries. The company produces a range of medical devices and data management tools. They have always been a market leader and commanded premium pricing; however, intensified competitive pressure from lower-cost manufacturers and increased customer price sensitivity have negatively impacted margins and market share. In response, the CMO repositioned a portion of the high-end product line and led efforts to acquire and develop a lower-cost product line. While the expanded portfolio is robust, the product lines lack differentiation, creating customer confusion and impacting financial performance. Product development, marketing, and sales are managed at the product level. Concerned that product overlap would further erode market share and profitability, Aaron engaged Deloitte to develop a new portfolio strategy and redefine the go-to-market strategy.
prompt.question: You are a Senior Consultant on the Deloitte team. Help DevCo address the following questions one at a time: (1) What factors should DevCo consider when evaluating its product portfolio and go-to-market strategy? (2) There are three primary product lines (A, B, and C). Which product line is most attractive for DevCo? (3) How many units of NewPro does DevCo need to sell to be profitable, and would you launch NewPro? (4) What should DevCo consider when deciding to launch NewPro for Product Line B? If you were the CEO, would you launch NewPro?

clarifying_info.q: What are the financial figures for each product line?
clarifying_info.a: See the data sheet (Exhibit 1). Revenue, COGS, and SG&A for 2011 and 2012 are provided for Product Lines A, B, and C, along with estimated 2013 growth rates and product line qualitative information. All costs are variable.

clarifying_info.q: What are the economics of NewPro?
clarifying_info.a: NewPro has a suggested price of $200 with a $15 rebate per unit. Manufacturing cost is $115 per unit and per-unit marketing costs are $20. Fixed costs to launch are $20,000,000. Product Line leadership only wants to launch if it is profitable by end of Year 1.

clarifying_info.q: What type of product is NewPro?
clarifying_info.a: NewPro will be positioned as 'leading edge' with a high-touch support model. It will be sold through the third-party distributors that Product Line B currently utilizes.

exhibits.title: DevCo Data Sheet
exhibits.shows: Financial data (Revenue, COGS, SG&A) for Product Lines A, B, and C for 2011 and 2012, estimated 2013 revenue growth rates, cost of capital figures (treat as extraneous), and a product line information table showing features/functionality, support model description, product life, sales channel, and price point for each line.

A.support: Always on call; high touch approach

C.support: Always on call; limited on-site availability

framework: Customer Mix: Understand types of customers and what attributes/engagement approach they require
Competition: Identify differentiators vs. lower-cost competitors and how to protect/gain share
Brand: Determine how to position products (features, price, channel) to maintain the DevCo brand
Channel: Evaluate distribution channels and relevant regulatory considerations
Product: Assess customer willingness to pay for features and which products are 'good enough'
Financial Impact: Determine revenue and profitability of each product line
Strategic Priorities: Align portfolio positioning with DevCo's goal of continued market leadership
Organization Structure: Assess whether current org can support future portfolio strategy
Global Footprint: Consider country-specific needs and regulatory impacts on product/GTM
Evolving Environment: Account for trends like Health Care Reform and emerging market growth

questions.prompt: What factors should DevCo consider when evaluating its product portfolio and go-to-market strategy?
questions.guidance: A good answer explores external environment and internal capabilities across: customer mix, competition, brand positioning, channel strategy, product features/willingness-to-pay, and financial impact by line. A great answer adds strategic priorities (market leadership, broad portfolio), organization structure feasibility, global footprint/regulatory considerations, and evolving market trends (ACA, emerging markets).

questions.prompt: Which product line (A, B, or C) is most attractive for DevCo? Build income statements for each line.
questions.guidance: Candidate should build income statements for 2012 (good) and ideally 2011-2013 (great). Cost of capital is extraneous — do not use. Calculate Operating Income = Revenue - COGS - SG&A and Operating Margin % = Operating Income / Revenue. Good answer: In 2012 alone, B has highest absolute operating income ($325M) but C has highest margin (38%). Great answer: Using 3-year view including 2013 forecast, C is most attractive on both total operating income AND margin due to its fast growth (50%), while B has slowest growth (5%) and declining margins. Qualitative: Product Line B's distributor model with limited support and commodity positioning drives lower margins; Line C's always-on support at a low price may reflect a favorable cost structure.

math.setup: 2013 Revenue = 2012 Revenue × (1 + growth rate); since all costs are variable, operating income grows at same rate as revenue. Operating Income 2013 = Operating Income 2012 × (1 + growth rate).
steps: Product Line A 2013: Rev=$1,200M, COGS=$720M, SGA=$180M, Op Inc=$300M, Margin=25%
Product Line B 2013: Rev=$2,363M, COGS=$1,785M, SGA=$236M, Op Inc=$341M, Margin=14%
Product Line C 2013: Rev=$900M, COGS=$375M, SGA=$180M, Op Inc=$345M, Margin=38%
3-year Operating Income totals: A=$830M, B=$1,046M, C=$715M
In 2013, C has highest Op Inc ($345M) and highest margin (38%)
math.answer: Product Line C is most attractive: highest operating margin (38%) in 2012-2013 and overtakes B in absolute operating income by 2013 due to 50% revenue growth vs. B's 5%.

questions.prompt: How many units of NewPro does DevCo need to sell to break even (be profitable by end of Year 1)?
questions.guidance: Straightforward breakeven calculation. Candidate must correctly subtract the rebate from price to get net price, identify all variable costs, calculate contribution margin, then divide fixed costs by contribution margin. A fair answer shows correct setup with minor arithmetic error.

math.setup: Net Price = Listed Price - Rebate. Variable Cost = Manufacturing + Marketing. Contribution Margin = Net Price - Variable Cost. Breakeven Units = Fixed Costs / Contribution Margin.

questions.prompt: Based on the breakeven analysis and prior considerations, would you launch NewPro?
questions.guidance: Good answer: Assess viability of selling 400,000 units in Year 1. One check: NewPro breakeven revenue = 400,000 × $185 = $74M, which is ~3.3% of Product Line B's 2012 revenue of $2,250M — suggesting breakeven is achievable. Good answer also references brand, selling model, and risk from Q1 analysis. Great answer additionally considers: impact on broader business (capacity, resourcing), product overlap concerns (NewPro as 'leading edge' is more similar to Line A, risking cannibalization/confusion), sales model mismatch (B uses distributors with limited support but NewPro needs high-touch), and whether rebate execution will be 100%. Candidate may note NewPro margin (27% on net price vs. B's 14%) is accretive to Line B. Great answer also considers mitigation: launching NewPro under Product Line A instead (better fit with features and sales force), or launching only if current B customers are demanding this product to prevent switching.

math.setup: NewPro breakeven revenue vs. Product Line B total revenue.
math.answer: Breakeven revenue is only ~3.3% of Line B revenue, suggesting volume target is achievable. However, qualitative factors (product overlap, support model mismatch, better fit with Line A) suggest caution or repositioning to Line A.

questions.prompt: What should DevCo consider when deciding to launch NewPro from a CEO (all three product lines) perspective? Would you launch?
questions.guidance: Good answer: Investment priorities — Line B has slow growth and low margins; Line C is most attractive, so investment should focus there. Product overlap — NewPro is 'leading edge' which conflicts with Line B's mid/entry positioning and is more similar to Line A, exacerbating the portfolio overlap problem. Support model — Line B uses distributors with limited on-site support; NewPro needs high-touch, requiring additional DevCo investment. Recommendation: Do not launch with current plan. Great answer: Mitigation strategies — consider launching NewPro under Line A (better feature and channel fit), determine if B customers are demanding NewPro to prevent switching, analyze whether direct sales force for Line A is an appropriate channel for NewPro.

recommendation: Product Line C is the most attractive line for DevCo given its highest operating margins (~38%) and fastest revenue growth (50% estimated for 2013), making it the priority for investment
NewPro should not be launched under Product Line B as currently planned due to support model mismatch, product overlap risks, and better strategic fit with Product Line A
risks: Launching NewPro under Line B risks further portfolio confusion and cannibalization of Line A revenues
Over-investing in Line B (slow growth, low margin) diverts resources from the more attractive Line C
If NewPro is not launched at all, current Line B customers demanding leading-edge products may switch to competitors
next_steps: Evaluate launching NewPro under Product Line A where feature set and high-touch sales force are better aligned
Conduct customer research to determine whether current Line B customers are actively demanding a leading-edge product
Develop a portfolio rationalization roadmap that reduces overlap between Lines A, B, and C
Consider organizational restructuring away from product-level silos to enable a more integrated customer-facing strategy
